policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: Qere וּמְרַ֥ק (lemma 4839) and ketiv ופרק (lemma 6564) are distinct lexemes, but both are the noun "broth"; פָּרָק is the broth of boiled fragments. ASV "and broth of abominable things is in their vessels" therefore renders either reading, and no note is mapped here.

Qere אֶל and ketiv על are the interchangeable prepositions of lemmas 413 and 5921 a. ASV "measure their former work into their bosom" is the idiom's ordinary English whichever preposition stands, so the wording does not distinguish them and no note is mapped here.
